findings.detail: The metadata probes inspect a symlink rather than its target. If input.json points to source.json, rendering input.json onto source.json compares different inode identities and replaces the underlying JSON with HTML. The mode probe likewise reads a symlink's permissions rather than its private target's permissions, potentially broadening access to the replacement page. These defects predate the range; the prior Important severity is preserved.
findings.evidence: The stat calls at lines 1363 and 1478-1479 omit -L. The installed stat manual documents lstat as the default and -L as selecting the target. Differing identities bypass line 1480, and write_output renames HTML onto source.json. The base revision contains the same executable statements. Existing tests cover direct paths only.
findings.title: Sibling input forms: metadata probes do not follow symlinks

findings.detail: Failure of both stat variants disables file protections while writing continues. With stat unavailable on PATH, replacing an existing 0600 page under umask 022 makes it 0644. Rendering with identical input and output paths also bypasses the identity guard and overwrites the JSON. These defects predate the range; the prior Important severity is preserved.
findings.evidence: Line 1363 converts failed probes to an empty mode; lines 1365-1367 substitute the current umask, which lines 1372-1373 apply before replacement. Lines 1478-1480 similarly skip the identity guard after failed reads. require_jq does not require stat. The base revision contains identical fallback behavior.
findings.title: Absent or partial data: failed metadata probes bypass file protections

findings.detail: The repository-mismatch diagnostic prints the complete origin URL. Gathering acme/widgets from a checkout whose origin is https://user:SECRET@github.com/acme/other.git therefore exposes the embedded credential on stderr. This defect predates the range; the prior Important severity is preserved.
findings.evidence: Line 1054 captures git remote get-url origin without sanitizing it. Lines 1055-1056 put that raw value into local-notice.txt, which lines 1336-1337 print to stderr. The sibling backlog-gather diagnostic names only the expected repository. The base revision contains the same raw-URL diagnostic.
findings.title: Untrusted data in commands: the origin diagnostic exposes URL credentials

findings.detail: Both gather helpers pass relative filenames beginning with a dash directly to jq. For example, backlog-gather finish -gather.json analysis.json output.json rejects an existing valid gather because jq interprets its filename as an option. bugs-gather repeats the problem for saved inputs and assessments. This defect predates the range; the prior Important severity is preserved.
findings.evidence: cmd_finish passes its arguments unchanged to require_json_file, whose line 327 supplies the path directly to jq. bugs-gather repeats this at lines 876 and 1394. report-board's operand function instead prefixes dash-leading filenames with ./, and its test covers that normalized path. The base revision has the same unnormalized gather readers.
findings.title: Sibling input forms: gather readers treat dash-leading filenames as options

findings.detail: A valid bugs board with repo acme/widgets accepts repoUrl https://git.example.com:99999/acme/widgets. Validation succeeds even though the port exceeds 65535, and rendering builds unusable repository, issue, pull-request and commit links from that address. This defect predates the range and is outside the changed lines.
findings.evidence: The bugs validator at line 600 accepts any nonempty digit sequence after the colon. The sibling backlog validator uses port_re to enforce 1 through 65535, with a regression assertion for port 99999. templates/bugs.html keeps repoUrl unchanged when URL parsing fails and appends /issues/, /pull/, /tree/ and /commit/ paths to it. The base revision contains the same permissive bugs validator.
findings.title: Validator gaps: bugs-board repository URLs accept invalid ports
